questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a country which had english as native language. University of Guelph also hade some interesting courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relative easy to find information of housing and some of the courses

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had an exchange team that we could email, they helped me sign up for courses. 
They also had a orientation days where we meet other exchange students. they showed us the school and where to buy books, but mostly focused on the social aspect. 
I had a really good RA which I could ask question about the residents and where to buy kitchen applies or the best cafe in town.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are dorm room for 1, 2 or 3, townhouses for 3 people and 1 bedroom apartment suite. When you are over 25 years, the campus housing consider you as mature student and you will be given one of the single apartment suite and not living in a community.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
In townhouse and 1 bedreoom apartment suite, there is a kitchen.  But some housing dont have, so you would have to have meal

They also have different meal plans depending on your need.
I had the flex one, where you can add more money on if needed. It's 500 cad at start. And still get 10% of when buying coffee or lucnch.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The kitchen only comes with fridge, freezer, oven and stove. You will have to buy or bring all kitchen supplies: pots, pans, plates etc.

All the international student lived at West village, which is around 15-20 minutes walk to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Would wished for an option of leaving my stuff for the next exchange student instead we had to find a thrift story and donate it there. And that i could have the same option instead of buying all new. 

They had a thrift store on campus but it opened 2 weeks after arrival.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a bit of strugglng due to some of the courses i wanted was at the same time, so i didnt get all course that i wanted.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to provide with a list of 8-10 courses that i would like to take, the exchange team from UoG will sign you up for the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The is a exchange team that help you sign up for classes. And when arriving on campus they also have counsiling that can help you if you change courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I didnt get all the courses i wanted, there was huge waitlist on some course. And some of them was at the same time. 
I also had to argument/fight for why I could take some of the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Always ask for help

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of 4th year courses was like at home. The 1st year was a lot of repetition of what I already learn back home, but it was nice to have an easy course and with focus on canada biodiversity instead.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style is different, a lot of lectures but not at all any reading or just very little. 
All assignemnt and quiz count to your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Zoo*4070 animal behaviour
Biol*4150 wildlife conservation & management
biol*4350 limnology of nat & pltd waters
biol*1070 discovering biodiversity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Animal behaviour was a really cool and I loved the teacher. You will get the change to conduct your own experiment so it takes up lot of time, but really worth it. 

4150 is more a R studio and programming course than i expected, still interesting topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy all kitchen supplies and beddings

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping a bit more expensive than I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They have so many clubs and social activities that you can sign up for. I signed up for the running club. 
But other student signed up for climbing, outdoor

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go to all the free stuff, i really recommend going to event in o-week and keep an eye on the app. 
Go to the bullring on Wednesday to open-mic

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go as often as you can! I went to Bruce peninsula, canoe trip in algonquin, Niagara falls both summer and winter, Arrowhead provincial park. 
Elora is also a cozy litlle town.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy, people are so friendly and helpful

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to the social gathering and sign up for a club. ADont be afraid to go alone. 
I also meet local student with all the group work in our classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Not really that much differens. I had to get used to tipping all te times. 
I had a bit difficult with remembering that taxes is not included in the prices, so you had too add it mentally so you would know the final prices before buying

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are so welcoming and also ready for a small talk, i missed that now.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go outside your comfort zone. Remember to have fun. Make sure to gon on trips on weekends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can pass with a grade of 50%.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friends i made and all the trips we did together - all the memories.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Finding time to do all the things i wanted, time fly by so fast. 
Being away from my friends and family

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
